title: NCEP ocean rainfall and evaporation fell together at 30S-30N after 2022 while their net flux changed little
abstract: We tested whether the cold SST boundary in the two NCEP reanalyses is linked to a change in their water cycle. We used monthly precipitation, latent heat flux and SST on a fixed open-ocean mask, with GPCP 2.3 and CMAP Standard rainfall references. In a 2000-2026 fit with trend, observed SST and ENSO controls, the 2022-23 transition gives a rainfall decrease relative to the references of 0.208-0.211 mm/day in R1 and 0.292-0.295 mm/day in R2 at 30S-30N. Model evaporation and rainfall fell by similar amounts. Their difference changed by only -0.009 and +0.020 mm/day. The point estimates cancel 96% and 94% of the rainfall change in net surface freshwater flux; joint block intervals put cancellation at 65-100% and 75-100%. The rainfall loss stays negative under tested fit and mask choices. Its spatial relation to the SST error stays positive within latitude bands. Period means show a larger loss, while differences partly recover in 2025. R1 analysed column water rises. A file served as R2 column water repeats R1 values and is excluded. These results show that net freshwater flux can hide a large change in gross model water cycling. They support a response to the faulty SST boundary but do not establish its causal share. Shared inputs, interim rainfall data, uncertain evaporation, short recent coverage and the lack of a controlled model rerun limit attribution.
